items.headline: Wall Street heads into a heavy week with a shaky AI rally
items.note: Stocks ended last week lower, with worries about financing heavy AI spending in the background. This week brings the Fed, earnings from 542 large companies, and Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon reports. Those results will show whether AI spending is paying off.

items.headline: Fed decides Wednesday; a hold at 3.75%-4.00% is expected
items.note: Futures price about a 91% chance the Fed holds rates, with Chair Kevin Warsh speaking at 2 p.m. ET. Thursday adds the first Q3 GDP estimate and core PCE inflation. Rates affect both the stock market and how much companies hire.

items.headline: Anthropic's draft IPO filing reportedly shows an $80.7B loss, mostly non-cash
items.note: Per WSJ/Reuters recaps, first-half 2026 revenue was $16.3B, up from $1.1B a year earlier. About $72B of the loss is non-cash accounting charges, and the filing reportedly lists about $450B in cloud commitments. These are secondhand reports of a draft, not a public filing.

items.headline: OpenAI's Decisions API is generally available
items.note: It returns probabilities, choices or scores instead of generated text, and OpenAI says it is up to 10x faster than using Luna through the Responses API. Cheap classification-style calls like this are a practical way to use LLMs in data pipelines.

items.headline: AI found two decades-old PHP flaws; NSA says patch now
items.note: The bugs date to PHP 5 (2004) and were found with AI tools including GPT-5.6 Sol. Details leaked before the fix, and several European and Australian government sites went offline. Fixes are out in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35.

items.headline: Report: Nvidia B300 chips seen on China Telecom-linked network
items.note: Israeli firm Lava reportedly spotted 32 B300 GPUs, which are barred from China, on monitoring endpoints tied to China Telecom. The data does not show where the chips physically are. Export-control enforcement shapes Nvidia's China business.

items.headline: Modal raises $750M at a $16B valuation
items.note: The serverless GPU platform passed a $1B run rate, per an AI news digest. It raised this Series D five months after a $5B Series C. Demand for AI infrastructure is still creating jobs.

items.headline: Data science hiring looks steady, and New York is a top market
items.note: One analysis of 12,148 US data science postings (updated July 2026) finds about 828 new postings a week, with New York at 14% of postings, behind California at 19%. Most are mid-level or senior, so internships are a harder niche to find.

items.headline: Canva releases Craft, its first in-house image model
items.note: Canva says it ranks second among AI labs for image generation on DesignArena's leaderboard. It is available through Dream Lab and the API. A sign that application companies are now training their own models.

learn.explain: A basis point (bp) is one hundredth of a percentage point, so 25 bp is 0.25%. Traders use it because rate changes are small and 'up a quarter point' is ambiguous. Fed funds futures are contracts whose prices move with what traders expect the Fed's rate to be, so people turn them into odds. This week, futures put about a 91% chance on the Fed holding at 3.75%-4.00%. A hold that is fully expected usually moves markets little; the surprise is more likely to come from the Fed chair's tone.
learn.try: Search for CME FedWatch and see how the odds change before Wednesday.
